$comment: Profile-driven camera definitions. The app renders its Image Settings UI
entirely from this file - add/remove/reorder entries here and the UI follows.
Field names under 'key' must match the firmware's JSON keys exactly,
including any firmware typos (e.g. 'drc_strenght').
'fastCmd' is optional. When present, dragging that slider fires an immediate
single-parameter write so you get live feedback in the preview. Everything is
still committed as a whole object when you press Apply.
engine: 'ffmpeg' pipes raw frames from an ffmpeg subprocess; 'vlc' uses the
embedded libvlc engine. ffmpeg is the default because libvlc refuses to show a
live picture below ~300 ms of buffering on this camera family, which puts a
floor under preview latency. ffmpeg has no such floor.
ffmpegPath is resolved next to the executable first, then on PATH. If it is
missing the app falls back to the VLC engine unless fallBackToVlc is false.
extraInputArgs are inserted before -i, e.g. [ "-max_delay", "0" ].

$comment_subnets: The /24 prefixes the app watches. This is the ENTIRE search scope - local
interface subnets are never added implicitly, so the app can only ever reach
a network named here. Add or remove entries and restart.
The app re-scans these continuously and keeps the camera list live:
continuous          - keep sweeping in the background
missesBeforeRemoval - consecutive misses before a camera is dropped; it is
shown as offline first, so a blip does not make rows
$comment_reachability: A subnet can only be searched if this machine has an address on it. At startup,
and whenever the subnet list changes, any unreachable subnet is detected and the
app offers to borrow a temporary address on the chosen adapter.
autoConfigureInterface - false only reports the problem and changes nothing
interfaceAlias         - empty picks the adapter already carrying the most
addresses, which on a multi-homed machine is the one
temporaryHostFirst/Last- host numbers searched for a free address; each
candidate is ping- and TCP-probed before it is used
Adding an address needs administrator rights, so Windows prompts once for the
whole batch. Existing addresses are never touched, and anything added is removed
when the app closes - or on the next start if it was killed before it could.
discovery.$comment_defaults: Always probed as well, so a camera on a factory-default address outside the swept range is still found.

$comment: Parameter files exported from a configured camera. Anything dropped in this
folder appears in the preset list, and the folder is watched, so it updates
without restarting.
A parameter file is always applied WHOLE, addressing included. Only files made
by Export carry a network block; the shipped Generic preset deliberately does
not, so applying it never moves a camera.

profiles.name: Vatilon H82 / Hi3516CV610

$comment_paths: VERIFIED BY DECODING, not by DESCRIBE. This firmware answers every RTSP
path with a byte-identical canned SDP and silently falls back to the SUB
stream for anything it does not recognise - so a path can look fine, play
fine, and still be the wrong stream. Only /stream1 and
Confirmed by changing each stream's codec and watching which path followed.
$comment_caching: Do NOT set below 300. Measured on this camera: at 100 ms the picture
freezes on the first frame while libvlc keeps decoding normally, on both
TCP and UDP - it looks exactly like a broken preview. 300 ms and above is
live. The app clamps this to 300 regardless of what is set here.

$comment_modes: Labels and values taken from the camera's own web UI, not invented:
view/network_setting.html maps each <option value> to a Tag id, and
lang/en-us.js resolves it. The tag ids are NOT in value order - value 1 is
Tag2224 while value 2 is Tag2220 - so each was resolved individually.
Both fields are timed enums, not booleans. A camera left on a subnet whose
gateway stops answering will, with adaptive enabled, give up its static
address after the interval below and take a DHCP lease instead - which is
how 192.168.144.53 moved itself to another subnet on 2026-08-14.
Set both to Disable to pin a camera in place.
network.$comment_readonly: Audited on hardware: dns, dns2, qwt_enable and qwt_ip_adaptive_mode all take. 'auto_dns' is reported but always reverts, and 'mac' is an identifier - both are stripped from parameter files. addr/netmask/gateway/dhcp_mode were not audited because changing them drops the connection by design; the app exercises them through the Network tab instead. qwt_ip_adaptive_mode moved out of passthroughKeys once the Network tab gained an explicit control for it.

$comment_detectors: The three event sources share one object shape: enable, duration, an 'output'
linkage bitmask, three work-mode enums and a 7-entry schedule. They differ
only in the extra fields each carries and which linkage bits its page offers.
All verified live on 192.168.144.54.
Read  mod=<module>&cmd=get, write mod=<module>&cmd=set with the whole object
in param. No channel is involved in any of them.
Labels come from the camera's own view/*.html resolved through lang/en-us.js.
Three traps were confirmed by reading the firmware, not assumed:
1. The work-mode select lists value 4 FIRST, then 0,1,2. Resolving those
positionally labels 'Close' as 'Work day' and shifts everything.
2. Schedule index 0 is SUNDAY. jquery.timeplan.js emits day='0' labelled
星期日. Each page's own lan{} block lists monday first, which is not the
wire order and would produce a seven-way off-by-one.
3. The output BIT is authoritative, not the stored work mode. Every page does
'if ((output >> bit) & 1) show the mode, else show Close'. This camera
stores voice_work_mode 2 with the voice bit clear, so trusting the mode
would silently switch the sound linkage on at the next save.
'threshold' is in pd and md but no page exposes it, so it is read and written
back untouched rather than surfaced.
vd (vehicle) and tp (tripwire) answer on this firmware but their
system_function bits are clear, so those features do not exist on this unit.

detectorDefaults.$comment_days: Order is the wire order: index 0 = Sunday.
detectorDefaults.$comment_workmodeouts: Each sets its own output bit whenever the mode is not Close, exactly as the firmware pages do. capabilityBit gates the control against device.system_function.

profiles.$comment_output: output bitmask: (ftp<<7)|(track<<6)|(light<<5)|(voice<<4)|(alarm_out<<3)|(email<<2)|(snapshot<<1)|client. Bit 6 (tracking) is gated on system_function bit 4, which is clear on this unit, so it is offered by no detector here.

detectors.label: Motion
detectors.$comment: Same page furniture as person detect; motion_detect.html offers the same four linkage checkboxes.

detectors.label: Alarm in
detectors.$comment: alarm_in.html offers only Send Message and Send Email - its output expression in alarm_in_setting.js has no ftp or snapshot term at all, so those bits are never set here.

detectors.label: Vehicle
detectors.$comment: NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE. system_function bit 26 is clear on the H82 available here, so this detector is hidden and its writes have never been exercised. Shape and labels come from a live read of mod=vd plus view/vehicle_detect.html; it is identical to pd except 'show_label' replaces 'show_human'.

detectors.label: Perimeter
$comment: NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE - system_function bit 21 is clear here.
Its payload genuinely has no light/voice/alarm-out work-mode fields, hence
suppressWorkModes. This covers the INTRUSION AREA mode only (mod=tp&cmd=get,
rectangles). The TRIP WIRE mode is a different object behind cmd=gettrip
carrying a two-point line, and needs a line-drawing surface the region
editor does not provide - deliberately not built.

detectors.label: Sound
detectors.$comment: NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE - system_function bit 12 is clear here. Its payload has light_work_mode and alarm_out_work_mode but no voice_work_mode, so the shared set is overridden rather than suppressed. No region.

$comment_modules: Plain settings modules, rendered from this list rather than hand-built XAML.
Every field below was read from a live camera (192.168.144.54); nothing here
is guessed from a page that the firmware might not implement.
A dotted key reaches into a nested object: 'ntp.server' is systime.ntp.server.
Fields the camera reports but that are not listed are read and written back
untouched, so nothing is lost by leaving something out.
NOTE the naming trap: the EMAIL settings live in the module called
'alarm_out' (email_setting.js:67). It is NOT the alarm-output relay - that is
alarm_out_work_mode inside each detector. Wiring a relay control to this
module would destroy the mail configuration.

modules.label: Time
modules.note: The camera stamps the OSD and every alarm from this clock.
modules.$comment_readonly: time_sec is the current epoch reading, not a setting. Capturing it into a preset and replaying it would set every camera's clock to the moment the preset was taken.

modules.label: Recording
modules.$comment: The key is 'mode', not 'record_mode'. Labels Tag1608/Tag1609.

modules.label: Privacy mask
modules.regionPrompt: Drag on the picture to draw a privacy mask. Up to 4; masked areas are blanked in the stream and in recordings.
modules.$comment: Same rect encoding as the detectors: normalised 0-10000 across the frame, fixed-length array with unused entries zeroed.

modules.label: Email
modules.note: This is the module the firmware calls 'alarm_out'. It is the mail configuration, not the alarm relay.

modules.label: Audio in
modules.$comment: audio is two objects behind two command pairs, not one. The vendor page writes every field here via set_input, then sends volume alone via set_output - hence the separate 'Audio out' entry. 'multi_input' is reported but the page never exposes it, so it is written back untouched.

modules.label: Audio out
modules.note: The camera's own page only ever sends the output volume; the other output fields follow the input settings.

modules.label: RTSP
modules.note: Changing the port moves the stream URL; this app's preview follows it on the next connect.

modules.label: Snapshot
modules.$comment: Per-channel, like osd. It answers a channel-less read but rejects a channel-less write with 'param num error'.

modules.label: Timed snapshot
modules.note: Snapshots on a timer, sent wherever the intervals below are set. Separate from snapshots taken on an alarm.

modules.label: HTTP
modules.note: The port this app and the camera's own web page are served on. Changing it drops the connection; reconnect on the new port.

modules.label: Cloud (P2P)
modules.$comment: p2p_id and qrcode are this camera's identity and status is live telemetry - all three are stripped from parameter files so a preset never clones one camera's cloud identity onto another.

modules.label: GB28181
modules.$comment: sip_user_id, sip_user_name and channel_id identify THIS camera to the platform. Replaying them onto a second camera registers two devices under one id, so they are stripped from parameter files - the server details and credentials still travel.
modules.note: Server settings travel in a preset; this camera's own SIP id and channel id do not, since they must stay unique.

$comment: Read:  mod=osd&cmd=get   with the channel in param2 (GetChannelAsync).
Write: mod=osd&cmd=set   with the channel in param, payload in param2.
Verified live on 192.168.144.54; omitting param2 on the read returns
'param num error'. There is no osd_ability module - the firmware exposes no
font, size or colour options, so none are offered here.
chn_num is 1 and channel 1 echoes channel 0, so no channel selector.
Labels and values are taken from the camera's own view/osd_setting.html and
resolved tag by tag through lang/en-us.js. Position 4 ('Hidden', Tag1908) is
commented out in the firmware's own page, so it is not offered.
The vendor page writes ONE position to all five text lines (sel_osd_pos),
even though the JSON carries a pos per line - this follows that, since it is
the behaviour the firmware is known to accept.
osd.$comment_readonly: no_save is a transport flag, not a setting - the firmware's own page never sends it.

$comment: 'bit' is tested against the camera's venc_set capability mask, so only
codecs the hardware actually supports are offered. 'value' is what gets
written to enc_type.
video.$comment_readonly: Audited on hardware: enc_type, width/height, framerate, gop, rc_mode, bitrate and quality all take. 'smart_enable' is reported but always reverts, so it is stripped from parameter files.
video.$comment_labels: Rate control and quality labels taken from the camera's own video settings page rather than invented.

system.$comment: Reboot and factory reset are the SAME module and differ by one word - 'reboot' keeps settings, 'reset' erases everything including the IP address. Named here so neither is ever assembled from a string at the call site.

$comment_readonly: Audited on hardware by writing each field individually and reading it
back. These two are reported by the firmware but never accept a value:
led_brightness - the live measured IR level, discarded in auto AND
manual LED mode. max_led_brightness is the real knob.
rotation       - only 0 is ever kept on this sensor; use mirror+flip.
They are stripped from exported parameter files so a preset carries only
settings that do something when replayed.
30 of the 35 fields the firmware reports are settable; day_begin/day_end
are structures and are carried through untouched.

settings.$comment: 'rotation' is deliberately absent: the firmware reports it but silently discards every value except 0, on this sensor. Use mirror and flip together for 180 degrees.
settings.label: Mirror (horizontal flip)

$comment: 'exposure' is the SHUTTER TIME, not an auto/manual flag - the web UI
builds this list at runtime from tv_standard, so the values mean
different speeds under PAL and NTSC. optionsFrom/optionSets
reproduces that: change TV standard and this list rebuilds.
The fastest step is gated to hi3516cv610/cv608 in the firmware, so
it is gated here too rather than offering a speed the sensor refuses.
settings.label: Exposure time

settings.$comment: Only Off/On, matching image_setting3 - the page this firmware actually uses (proven: it accepts cmd=set_single, which only that page issues). The older image_setting page offers a third value 2 = Auto; the camera stores it, but it is not offered here because this firmware's own UI does not.
settings.label: WDR

settings.$comment: AGC is a gain CEILING, not a low/medium/high setting - the firmware offers automatic plus powers of two up to 512x.
settings.label: AGC gain limit

settings.$comment: Checked against the firmware's own list: 0 is Auto and 1 is Always Day. An earlier version of this file had those two swapped.
settings.label: Day/Night mode

settings.$comment: Measured range is 1-5. 0 clamps up to 1, values above 5 clamp down to 5.
settings.label: Switch sensitivity

settings.$comment: The firmware lists this as plain levels 0-10 with no units, so it is shown as a level rather than invented second values.
settings.label: IR-cut delay level

settings.$comment: 'led_brightness' is deliberately absent: the firmware always reports the live measured level and discards writes, in both auto and manual LED mode. 'max_led_brightness' is the knob that works.
settings.$comment2: Checked against the firmware: 0 is automatic and 1 is manual. An earlier version of this file had these inverted.
settings.label: IR LED mode

settings.$comment: Firmware list. The earlier Auto/Manual/Indoor/Outdoor labels were invented - 2 is a lock, and 3-6 are light-source presets.
settings.label: White balance

settings.$comment: The web UI presents these as one three-way control: off, or on at weak/strong strength. It is NOT a mains-frequency selector - the earlier 50/60 Hz labels here were wrong. Mains frequency is tv_standard.
settings.label: Anti-flicker
